records.title: Equivalent Comparisons of Experiments
supports: For a fixed decision problem, a Blackwell-more-informative experiment has weakly greater optimized expected value.
limitations: Does not compare policies that optimize different objectives or decision problems whose feasible strategies change with the experiment.

records.title: The critical probability of bond percolation on the square lattice equals 1/2
records.publisher: Springer Science and Business Media LLC
supports: Independent bond percolation on the infinite square lattice has open-edge critical probability 1/2.
limitations: Does not by itself prove finite-torus giant-component size, finite-size rates, or welfare consequences.

records.title: Sharpness of the phase transition in percolation models
records.publisher: Springer Science and Business Media LLC
supports: Subcritical independent percolation has exponential decay in the sharpness regime covered by the paper.
limitations: The exact cluster-size-tail form used by a manuscript claim must still match the cited theorem and model convention.

records.title: Percolation
records.evidence_locator: Second edition; manuscript cites Theorem 6.75 and Sections 8.2-8.3.
supports: Standard infinite-lattice subcritical and supercritical percolation results at the cited locations.
limitations: A book citation does not automatically establish the manuscript's finite-torus asymptotics or its welfare translation.

records.title: Surface order large deviations for Ising, Potts and percolation models
records.publisher: Springer Science and Business Media LLC
records.evidence_locator: Percolation large-deviation results in large finite regions.
supports: Finite-volume supercritical percolation admits surface-order large-deviation control under the paper's hypotheses.
limitations: The citation is not treated as an automatic proof of the manuscript's all-p-above-critical square-torus statement.

records.title: Minimizing a Submodular Function on a Lattice
records.publisher: Institute for Operations Research and the Management Sciences (INFORMS)
records.evidence_locator: Lattice comparative-statics results under submodularity/supermodularity hypotheses.
supports: Monotone comparative statics follows when the required lattice and increasing-differences hypotheses are established.
limitations: Does not establish increasing differences for the Blackwell Dilemma welfare function; that premise is paper-specific.

records.title: A critical point for random graphs with a given degree sequence
records.evidence_locator: Critical-point criterion for random graphs with a prescribed degree sequence.
supports: Under the source's regularity hypotheses, the excess-degree criterion determines giant-component emergence.
limitations: Requires checking degree-sequence regularity, finite-size cutoffs, and the translation from retention to blocking probability.

records.title: Resilience of the Internet to Random Breakdowns
records.evidence_locator: Random-failure threshold analysis for heavy-tailed networks.
supports: The asymptotic random-failure threshold approaches complete removal for an idealized infinite-variance degree law.
limitations: Does not cover targeted removal and does not imply that every vertex lies in the giant component or has vanishing topological loss.

records.title: Random graphs with arbitrary degree distributions and their applications
supports: For the covered random-graph model, the first two degree moments determine the giant-component threshold.
limitations: Does not establish the paper's welfare conclusions without a separate component-size-to-welfare argument.

records.title: Random Graphs
records.evidence_locator: Second-edition Erdos-Renyi component-size and giant-component results.
supports: For G(n,c/n), component-size behavior changes at c=1, with a linear giant component for c>1.
limitations: The citation supplies random-graph premises, not the Blackwell Dilemma welfare mapping.

records.title: Good things peak in pairs: a note on the bimodality coefficient
supports: The 5/9 value is a diagnostic benchmark for the sample bimodality coefficient.
limitations: The diagnostic does not prove multimodality or any theorem-level economic claim.

records.title: Correlation-length exponent in two-dimensional percolation and Potts model
supports: The value nu=4/3 is used as a finite-size-scaling diagnostic for two-dimensional percolation.
limitations: The exponent is diagnostic input here and is not a machine proof of finite-size collapse or manuscript theorem closure.
